REFUTED on its universal quantifier, though its arithmetic is exact. I re-ran the md5 cross-product myself: 27 web files, 42 android files, 21 exact matches, and the enumerated 'Full identical set' in the quote is correct file-for-file - including md5 6852a591ab2d5895090b3d37ccec9ba2 for BOTH bindata/103_1t4630s0.bin and android/94_MCSCharacter_Human2AnimationData.bin. But 'including the ENTIRE character-animation layer' is measurably FALSE, and it is the clause the lane_impact hangs on ('the animation data layer needs NO build hedge at all'). Five web animdata blobs have NO android byte-twin and differ in CONTENT, not just bytes: 100_1t4627s0.bin (ogre) has 20 <anim> in 184,193 B vs android 91_Ogre's 18 in 184,120 B; 102_1t4629s0.bin (skills - shunpo, deathtouch, fireball) 51 anims in 333,768 B vs android 93_Skills 51 in 338,096 B; 111_1t4638s0.bin 17 vs android 102_Guardian 16; 113_1t4640s0.bin 26 anims / 153,258 B vs android 104_HumanSpear 23 / 132,270 B; 114_1t4641s0.bin (10 anims) unmatched entirely. So the animation layer is 14 of 19, not 'entire', and the two most gameplay-load-bearing sets (skills and ogre) are precisely the exceptions. The hedge lifts for the 21 named files ONLY. Corrected version supplied in new_findings so the good measurement is not lost.

The same *0.1 scale appears in the reach switch (:3105, :3116), so the correction propagates to reach as well.
